title: Freetown Christiania
summary: Josh and Chuck explore Freetown Christiania, the anarchist squatter commune in Copenhagen, Denmark, founded in 1971 when residents took over an abandoned military base. The episode covers the base's history and the neighborhood's origins, the community's self-imposed rules and garbage collection, its growth into a self-governed village with cafes, a kindergarten, and the Grey Hall venue, and the Pusher Street hash trade and biker gang violence (including the BS and Hells Angels war from 1983 to 1986). It also covers the residents' drug-control measures, the government's shifting stance and eviction threats, the 2011 land purchase through a foundation, the resident-run rent and fee system, the Christiania coin, the planned public housing, and the factions within the community. The episode ends with a listener email about Camp David.

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode on Freetown Christiania in Copenhagen.

segments.title: Military base history and the playground fence
segments.summary: Background on the Copenhagen fortress and artillery barracks, their closure by the military by 1971, and neighborhood parents tearing down fences so children could play there.

segments.title: Hovedstaden, the Christiania name and the 1971 article
segments.summary: Hosts discuss the Christianshavn neighborhood and the name Christiania, then describe editor Jacob Ludvigsen's 1971 counterculture newspaper article calling for the base to become an anarchist housing commune.

segments.title: Early rules, self-policing and garbage team
segments.summary: The early community forms rules, starting with no violence, enforced by social pressure and shunning, and forms a garbage team. Early businesses and facilities open.

segments.title: Culture, Grey Hall and artists
segments.summary: Overview of the community's cafes, shops, kindergarten and theaters, the Grey Hall venue and its concerts, and the artistic character of the neighborhood.

segments.title: Residents and musician Lucas Forshammer
segments.summary: Population of roughly 800 to 900 residents with about 150 children, and musician Lucas Forshammer of Lucas Graham, who was raised there.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Break before the next segment.

segments.title: Pusher Street and the biker gang war
segments.summary: Pusher Street became an open hash market despite cannabis being illegal, and harder drugs and criminal gangs (BS Motorcycle Club and Hells Angels) fought over it, including a gang war from 1983 to 1986.

segments.title: Drug economy, violence and police conflict
segments.summary: Estimates of the drug economy's share and value, a dismembered body found in 1987, and police campaigns. Residents struggled to push out dealers and gangs, and later shootings and a fatal stabbing occurred.

segments.title: Police efforts and the removal of Pusher Street
segments.summary: Police campaigns including a 1992 eighteen-month effort and a training replica of Pusher Street; residents' own tactics against dealers; Pusher Street was dug up and removed in 2024 with plans for housing.

segments.title: Residents' drug bans and hash boycott
segments.summary: Residents forced out heroin dealers in the late 1970s, introduced random urine testing for heroin users, and urged tourists to buy hash elsewhere. Tourism peaks in summer.

segments.title: Government relations and the Christiania Act
segments.summary: The government's shifting stance from a 1972 social experiment to a 1976 eviction order, court fights, rezoning in 1987, and the 1989 Christiania Act requiring licenses and certifications.

segments.title: 2011 land purchase and collective ownership
segments.summary: The 2011 agreement in which residents raised 12.5 million kroner through a foundation to buy part of the land and rent the rest, and the collective ownership model.

segments.title: Rent, fees and resident selection
segments.summary: Monthly rent of about four dollars and a maintenance fee of about 196 dollars; residents now go through interviews and fourteen neighborhood groups make decisions by consensus.

segments.title: Christiania coin and challenge coins
segments.summary: The community mints its own copper coin, the lune, with a pot leaf and snail design, and the hosts joke about getting a coin minted.

segments.title: Community rules list
segments.summary: Additional rules: no stealing, no bulletproof vests, no guns or knives, no gang colors, and no running during police raids.

segments.title: Current state, public housing plans and factions
segments.summary: Plans for public housing expected around 2029 divide residents. Sociologist Bergmann? divided residents into three strata: activists, liberalists, and a bottom group; the liberalists are credited with normalization.

segments.title: Travel banter and sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts discuss visiting Copenhagen and Scandinavia, then introduce listener mail.

segments.title: Listener mail: Troy's father at Camp David
segments.summary: Listener Troy shares that his father was a Marine captain stationed at Camp David from 1971 to 1973, where Troy learned to swim and kept memorabilia.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts invite listeners to send personal stories and close the show.
